reviews.title: Horrible App
reviews.text: I downloaded this app as I saw a clip of it and thought it would be something good to do with my 13m to have another avenue for her to learn words. I did the assessment at the start of the app which is worded in a way of seeing if the child is “hitting milestones” which all parents worry over anyway! Once I completed the assessment the phrase I was faced with completely blew me away “So, some not so good new and some good news” what terrible wording! To then follow with “The not so good news (child’s name) isn’t meeting their milestones” I think this app could be good but I deleted it instantly following that! Absolutely no consideration for how parents may feel!

reviews.title: Repeatedly prompted to restore purchases
reviews.text: I got this app for an autistic kiddo. It is a good app, except for two problems: it kept prompting me to restore a purchase I’d already made. When I’m trying to pull up the game with a child screaming desperately in my ear, this was understandably frustrating. The game would also freeze, causing more screaming. Go ahead and get this for your neurotypical child, sounds like it works for them, but I advise to avoid unless you want to see tantrums while trying to log in. Worse, it was entertaining but caused zero language gains for my kid. I reached out to support and received no reply, so that’s great too.

reviews.title: Evaluation score untrue +others
reviews.text:
I canceled my subscription the very next day after purchasing it because I was disappointed with the assessment system. The progress and levels did not appear to accurately reflect my child’s individual performance, and the scores seemed very similar regardless of how the child performed.

As a parent, I found this concerning because it can make you feel like your child is behind when the assessment may not actually be accurately measuring their abilities. I also questioned whether the testing system is designed in a way that could make the app appear more effective when a child performs better on a later test.

I would like to see more transparent and individualized assessments that clearly explain how a child’s score and developmental level are determined. I canceled because I did not feel the subscription was providing an accurate evaluation of my child.

reviews.title: A Free Trial I Can’t Even Use. Absolutely Shameful.
reviews.text:
I downloaded Speech Blubs yesterday and signed up for a 2-day free trial. Before subscribing, I was explicitly told my trial would end on the 21st.

Yet less than 24 hours later, I’m being presented with a 50% off subscription offer that I cannot find a way to decline.

I REFUSE to accept this offer. But now I can’t even use the app I downloaded to try in the first place!

My free trial has NOT expired. I was told it ends on the 21st. So why am I being blocked from using the app before that date?

I have barely had 24 hours to experience this product, and instead of allowing me to explore it, the app is pushing me toward a paid subscription. My card details are already on file, which makes this experience even more uncomfortable. The offer also took me away from the App Store.

This is not what I understood a free trial to be. A free trial should give customers the opportunity to experience the product and decide whether it is worth paying for. It should not mean being locked out of the experience before the advertised trial period is over.

Offering me 50% off before I’ve even had a reasonable chance to try the app is not an incentive. It’s an interruption that has completely undermined my confidence in the company.

I do not want the discount. I want access to the free trial I was promised.

The fact that I cannot find a way to decline this offer and continue using the app is absolutely unacceptable.

This has turned what should have been a straightforward trial into a frus

reviews.title: Nice Concept but costs $15 a month
reviews.text: I’m a professional who works with kids and it’s my opinion that, if you truly want to help nonverbal kids and their families, make this free, or at the most— $5 a month. Not many families can afford this. $15 a month may not seem like a lot to some people, but a lot of families with nonverbal kids are already paying a lot for therapies, respite, modified strollers, equipment designed for kids with special needs (because we all know that companies inflate the prices of anything with “special needs” or “neurodivergent friendly” associated with it), and much more. I will not be using this app when there are plenty of educational videos out there for free. I LOVE the idea of the app though and if the subscription costs less, I would use the app. But until then, definitely not using this app.

reviews.title: Poor trial period
reviews.text:
I can’t believe how little time this app allows you to test it out. We opened a few games to try and the trial time was over almost instantaneously. Sure, it lets you watch a movie for more usage a few times, but will literally only give you an extra 2 minutes. This kind of trial makes the users assume the app has zero content and the developers are just trying to get you into a subscription. 
Which gets me into the content. Is it actually curated by age group? Cause my 1 1/2 year old is not going to jump from knowing 5 basic words to saying “tractor” as his first lesson. I’ve had 3 kids, I know that’s not plausible. 
I REALLY wanted to try it out, per the reviews it sounded like a great investment, but I’m not paying $14 a month just to see if it actually gets better. 
Great concept, but maybe open up your trial to AT LEAST 1 day of full content use?
